messages:
maria-g: Quick q — our CI started failing when the pipeline runs the Redwood CLI in a container. The existing dev laptop script relied on the macOS keyring, which obviously isn't present in the build image. Any recommended patterns for non-interactive / ephemeral tokens in containers?

kevin-b: For containers we usually avoid keyring entirely. Two common patterns: 1) mount the secret as a file and read into an env var, or 2) inject as an env var from the runtime (K8s secret, GitHub Actions secret). Example we use: `export REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(cat /run/secrets/redwood_token)` then call `redwood login --token "$REDWOOD_TOKEN" --profile ci` or just set `REDWOOD_TOKEN` and let the CLI pick it up.

ashley: +1 to mount-as-file. We keep a tiny wrapper in CI so credentials don't leak into logs:
```bash
# ci-step.sh
set -euo pipefail
export REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(cat /run/secrets/redwood_token)
export REDWOOD_CLI_NONINTERACTIVE=1
redwood config use-profile ci || true
redwood models list --limit 1
```
That avoids any interactive prompt and prevents `redwood login` from trying to open a browser.

jonathan-l: FWIW: avoid trying to use OS keyrings in noninteractive images — they fail in weird ways. Also we've added `REDWOOD_CLI_NONINTERACTIVE=1` in a few places to silence prompts. If you need rotation, prefer short-lived tokens + a refresh step in the pipeline that pulls a rotated secret right before the job runs.

maria-g: Nice, thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) is there a safe way to refresh tokens mid-run (we have long-running services that sometimes need to re-auth without restarting), and 2) any gotchas around streaming APIs and tokens in CI?

kevin-b: For long-running processes, simplest reliable approach is file-backed tokens: mount a secret volume and update the file atomically (write to tmp + mv). Have your process watch the file mtime and reload token when it changes. If you can't change the process, schedule a short restart.

ashley: On streaming: short TTLs on tokens can cause streams to drop if the token expires mid-stream. Best practice: either use session tokens that are valid longer than the expected stream, or implement reconnect + resume semantics (client resumes from last event id). Also ensure the client re-reads token file/env on reconnect rather than caching forever.

cli-bot: :robot_face: infra-check — build #412 failed earlier due to expired token (fyi).

jonathan-l: Another small gotcha: some CI runners sanitize environment variables before running subprocesses — make sure the token variable is exported in the same shell/session the CLI runs in. And if you base64-encode tokens in your secret store, decode in the job before exporting.

maria-g: Perfect — I'll switch to mount-as-file + wrapper step and add a pre-job refresh. Will report back if we see stream disconnects. Thanks all :heart:
